And that if it were not for God's blessing upon us in this day which is stripped from the night, we would always be in darkness, and this is without doubt tiring to people and harmful to them. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then hear?"﴾ [al-Qasas 71].

Then He said: ﴿And the sun runs on to its resting place﴾ to the end of the verses.

* Among its benefits: the sun runs, that is, moves, and this is the reality. The apparent meaning of the noble Qur'an is that its motion is by its own nature, and it is not meant that it runs in the sense of appearance to the eye while the one that revolves is the earth. It is obligatory to take the Qur'an according to its apparent meaning until a clear proof is established that would be for us a proof before God, the Mighty and Majestic, if we depart from the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, because the one who spoke the Qur'an is the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, and He is the All-Knowing of His creation. So if He says that the sun runs, it is obligatory for us to say that the sun runs, and it is not permissible for us to say that we are the ones who run; rather, it is the sun that runs by the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

* Among its benefits: this sun, which is constantly and continuously moving, must have an end, by His saying: ﴿to its resting place﴾. Following from this, all creatures have an end: everything in this world of creatures has an end and will pass away: ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come out before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ibrahim 48].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: this sun is measured with a far-reaching, ordered measure, by His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾. This reality bears witness to it: from the time Allah created this sun until it ceases, it is in its orbit and does not advance or delay from the course which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded it to follow, and it does not rise or sink. It has even been said: if it sank by the width of a hair, it would burn the earth, and if it rose by the width of a hair, the earth would freeze. But God, the Mighty and Majestic, made it according to this wondrous, firm measure that does not change.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, namely: ﴿the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾. From them is derived the affirmation of two attributes that they include, namely might and knowledge. From them is also derived the affirmation of the effect or the judgement, which is that He overcomes everyone and knows everything.

* Among the benefits of the verse in His saying: ﴿And the moon — We have decreed for it stations﴾, among its benefits also: that this moon is a sign of the signs of God, the Mighty and Majestic, in that it is placed in its orbit, and yet it has stations which it descends to each night. It is not unrestricted, but it is measured by stations which it descends to each night. The wisdom of these stations is that people may know the number of years and the reckoning, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is He who made the sun a brightness and the moon a light and determined for it stations that you may know the number of years and the account﴾ [Yunus 5]. So much so that those who know the stations of the moon know the night of the month, even if they had not calculated from the beginning, on the basis of knowing the stations, because these stations do not change, and the moon's arrival at them also does not change. They are arranged by God, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of analogy (qiyas), by His saying: ﴿until it returns like the old dried palm-stalk﴾. Every simile or parable in the Qur'an indicates analogy, because a simile or parable is attaching one thing to another for a reason, which is called in rhetoric the aspect of comparison (wajh al-shabah).

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: applying the word "old" (qadim) to other than God, contrary to the philosophers who say: the most specific attribute of God is antiquity (qidam). This is wrong; if this were the most specific attribute of God, it would not be described by anything other than God. Antiquity does not indicate eternity (azaliyya). For this palm-stalk God described it as old, yet it is not, what? It is not eternal, since it is a created thing that did not exist before. Through this the falsity of the saying of those who claim that the most specific attribute of God, the Mighty and Majestic, is antiquity becomes clear. If they had said: the most specific attribute of God is primacy (awwaliyya), we would agree with what they said, because God is the First, before whom there is nothing. But to say that antiquity is the most specific attribute of God, while it is also applied to what is created, this is not possible and not correct.

* Also in it: there is evidence of God's power in respect of the light of the moon, for it begins weak, then increases in strength, then returns to weakness. This is from the power of God, the Mighty and Majestic, for if He willed He could make it always full and complete, or always deficient.

* Also among its benefits: an allusion to the state of man. When a person reflects upon the moon, he finds that it corresponds to the state of man, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is Allah who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾ [al-Rum 54]. The state of man is thus exactly equivalent to the state of the moon: the moon appears weak, then increases in strength, until when its strength is complete it begins to decline, and likewise man with respect to his life.

God, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night overtake the day﴾.

* In this verse there is evidence that the sunnah (law/pattern) of God, the Mighty and Majestic, does not change; this is the basic principle, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you will not find in the sunnah of Allah any alteration, and you will not find in the sunnah of Allah any transformation﴾ [Fatir 43]. So the sunnah of God, glorified and exalted, does not change in the universe. But is it a necessary sunnah, such that it is impossible for God to change it?

The answer: No. But God, the Exalted, has informed us that this sunnah does not change, yet it changes by His changing it. For this reason the sun was held back for Yusha' ibn Nun[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3124), and Muslim (1747/32), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], as came in the authentic hadiths. And for this reason too, when the Hour draws near, the sun will rise from where? From its place of setting. And for this reason the moon was split in the time of the Prophet ﷺ and became two halves[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3636), and Muslim (2800/43), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]]. These cosmic sunan do not alter and do not change, but God is able to alter or change them, and this would be for a cause.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the sun cannot rise at night. It cannot, according to the divine sunnah; but according to God's power, what? It is possible for it to rise at night, because God says: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: the night does not precede the day, so it does not enter upon it or come before it in such a way that two nights follow each other entirely: ﴿Nor does the night overtake the day﴾. This is what appears to us from this noble verse, and it may have a meaning other than what we understand from its outward form. For this reason, perhaps, those who study astronomy may see in this expression more than what has become clear to us.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: the sun, the moon, the night and the day are in an orbit — that is, in something circular like the whorl of a spindle — and they revolve; as He says: ﴿each in an orbit, swimming﴾.

* Among its benefits: the weakness of the saying of those who claim that the sun is in the fourth heaven and the moon in the lowest heaven, and who make the planets, the sun and the moon specific planets, each in a heaven, in this order from highest to lowest:
Zuhal, Sharā, his Mirrikh from his Shams, so Tazāharat with ʿUtārid the moons.
These are seven, each one in a heaven: Zuhal (Saturn) is the highest, in the seventh heaven, according to the words of the earlier astronomers; Sharā (Jupiter) in the sixth heaven; Mirrikh (Mars) in the fifth heaven; Shams (the sun) in the fourth heaven; Tazāharat (Venus) in the third heaven; ʿUtārid (Mercury) in the second heaven; al-Aqmār (the moon) in the lowest heaven. This verse contains the order of these planets:
Zuhal, Sharā, his Mirrikh from his Shams, so Tazāharat with ʿUtārid the moons.

(...) from the Book of God nor from the Sunnah of the Messenger of God ﷺ. We only know that these planets are above one another through eclipse: if the moon eclipses the sun, we know that it is beneath it, just as we know that cloud is beneath the sun because it screens it. And if the moon eclipses some of the stars, we know that it — that is, the moon — is beneath them. For this reason the moon eclipses all the stars, and the sun, and nothing eclipses it except the earth, because the earth is beneath it and blocks the light of the sun from it, and then it is eclipsed. I and others have witnessed that the moon eclipses some stars: you find it moving around them and then covering them. This shows that the moon is lower than the rank or height of these stars.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a refutation of the saying of those who claim that the sun is fixed and does not revolve. The strange thing is that they say it is fixed and that the moon revolves around the earth. This is an error, because God, glorified and exalted, made the ruling one: He said: ﴿each in an orbit, swimming﴾. So if we interpret swimming as revolving and affirm that for the moon, then let us affirm it for the sun too.

I have a word here which we have not explained from the author's commentary; he said: (they swim; they were given the status of rational beings).

(They were given the status of whom?) The sun, the moon, the night and the day (were given the status of rational beings), and that is by using the wāw which is for rational beings. The wāw is the plural pronoun, which only comes for rational beings; for non-rational beings the plural is with the feminine plural nūn. So if we want to add something to non-rational things in the plural, we use the feminine plural nūn; and for rational beings we use the wāw or the mīm. For example, you say: "the camels — their riders mounted them", not "the camels — their riders mounted them" with the mīm, because the mīm is for the rational. And you say: "the camels came (qadimna)" or "the camels drank (sharibna)", and you do not say "they drank" (sharibū), because the wāw here is for the rational. ﴿yasbahūn﴾ came with the wāw which is for the rational; he says: it has been given the status of a rational being by attributing swimming and moving to it, and moving only comes from one with will and reason.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 36, verses 37–40 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And a sign for them is the night﴾ [Ya-Sin 37]. We say concerning its grammatical analysis (i'rab) what we said concerning ﴿a sign for them is the earth﴾. So ﴿the night﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), and ﴿a sign﴾ is a predicate placed first (khabar muqaddam). And we say regarding the same wording what we said regarding His saying: ﴿We have revived it﴾, meaning that it is permissible for it to be a descriptive clause (sifah) modifying ﴿the night﴾, in the manner of the poet's saying:
"And indeed I pass by the base man, who abuses me..." ∗∗∗ ............................
And it is permissible for the sentence to be a resumptive, explanatory clause (isti'nafiyyah), explaining this sign: in what way was it a sign? In what way was the night a sign? He said: ﴿We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness﴾ [Ya-Sin 37]. "Nasliku" (We strip): the author says: (We separate). Allah named it "stripping" because it resembles the stripping of the hide from a beast (salkh al-jild min al-bahimah). ﴿We strip from it the day﴾, because the day is an existent matter that comes into being by the existence of the sun. It comes upon the night, so when the sun sets, this light follows it, like the hide that is stripped from a beast. When you strip the hide from a beast, you find it withdrawing little by little; likewise the day's light, like the night, Allah, exalted is He, strips the day from the night just as the hide is stripped from a beast. He said: ﴿then behold, they are in darkness﴾ [Ya-Sin 37]; that is, they have entered into darkness. "Idha" (then behold) is a particle of sudden occurrence (fa'iyyah), indicating that with the mere occurrence of this stripping, the atmosphere becomes dark. As we observe, the stripping comes little by little, but when the stripping is complete, the darkness is found complete. This is from the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for if pitch darkness came upon bright light, this would harm the eyes, the trees and many other things. But because it comes little by little, the matter descends from the highest degree of illumination to darkness gradually.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it﴾ [Ya-Sin 38]. The "wa" (and) is a conjunctive particle, and ﴿the sun﴾ is conjoined to ﴿the night﴾; meaning, and a sign for them is also the sun...
﴿runs on to a resting place for it﴾. It is permissible for the "wa" to be resumptive and for "the sun" to be a subject; both are permissible, but the first meaning is stronger.

He said: ﴿And the sun runs﴾ to the end of the verse, is part of the sign for them, or another sign. And likewise the moon. That is, whether we say the sentence is resumptive and that this is a new, separate sign, or we say the "wa" is a conjunctive particle, there is no doubt that the sun, in the attribute Allah mentioned, is indeed one of the signs of Allah. The sun is a sign of Allah in its very essence: this great, mighty body whose heat reaches the earth despite the vast distance between it and the earth. There is no doubt that this is one of the signs of Allah.

Who can create such a fiery, blazing, luminous mass whose light, rays and heat reach the earth across this enormous distance?

The answer: no one can. Therefore it is a sign of Allah. Then there are the benefits that arise from it: ripening fruits, warming the earth, and great light. How much energy does a person spare through the light of this sun in place of electricity? Great energy. Whether this is through the heat in the winter days, by which the sun makes the warming of houses unnecessary, or through the illumination, this is a matter that has no price. As for ripening fruits, drying dates and the like, in what serves the benefit of creation, "speak and there is no blame" (haddith wa la haraj). It is a sign of Allah, a great sign of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is also a sign in its course. He said: ﴿runs to a resting place﴾ [Ya-Sin 38]. "Tajri" means it moves in a course, and running (jary) is walking with intensity. Likewise the sun moves with an enormous speed, whose extent none knows except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, though it may be known by modern means the extent of its speed. But consider now: the airplane moves at great speed, and it is near us, is it not? It is near, yet we see it moving slowly because of its distance from us. So what of the sun? We observe it moving, there is no doubt about this; indeed, when you look at the shadow as it separates from the ray, you find it moving as if trembling, and this is evidence that it moves with a great movement. And despite this, how far is it from us? Very far. And we observe it moving this motion. Therefore its motion is very swift, and its measure is now known to astronomers.

As for His saying: ﴿to a resting place for it﴾, the author said: (That is, toward it, it does not exceed it). A "mustaqarr" is a place of settling, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And for you on the earth is a resting place and provision for a time﴾ [al-Baqarah 36], and He made the earth a settled place (qararan), so "al-mustaqarr" is the place of settling.

The author said: (That is, toward it, it does not exceed it). "Al-mustaqarr" is the place of settling, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And for you on the earth is a resting place and provision for a time﴾ [al-Baqarah 36], and He said: ﴿Who made the earth a settled place﴾ [al-Naml 61]. So "al-mustaqarr" is the place of settling. Allah, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its resting place and its place of storage﴾ [Hud 6]. So what is this settling toward which the sun runs: is it a temporal settling, a spatial settling, or both?

It is established in the authentic hadith from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was with the Prophet ﷺ in the mosque when the sun set, and he said: "Do you know where it goes?" Abu Dharr said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It goes and prostrates beneath the Throne and asks permission, and that is its resting place." Then he recited: ﴿And the sun runs to a resting place for it. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Ya-Sin 38]." [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3199) and Muslim (159 / 250), from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] Does this hadith indicate that its resting place is spatial or temporal? Spatial, because it prostrates beneath the Throne. We do not know the manner of this prostration, because the sun is not like humans, so that its prostration could be measured by human prostration; rather it is a greater creation, and we do not know how it prostrates. So the question does not arise for us: does it prostrate while moving, or does it stand still? And how is it valid to say that it prostrates and seeks permission while it still continues on the horizon? All these questions and objections we will answer, God willing, when mentioning the benefits.

It has also been said: the resting place is a temporal resting place, and that is at its folding up (takwir) on the Day of Resurrection; that is, at the end of its course on the Day of Resurrection. That is, it runs until the Day of Resurrection, which is its temporal place of settling.

It has also been said: the intended resting place is the limit of its movement among the northern and southern zodiacal signs. It has a limit it reaches in the north which it does not exceed, and a limit it reaches in the south which it does not exceed. On this basis the resting place is both temporal and spatial, because the furthest point of its course in the north is where the beginning of the summer season (al-qayz) occurs, and the furthest point of its course in the south is where the beginning of winter occurs. This is a resting place or settling that is temporal and spatial. So the sun, this great sun whose extent none knows except He who created it, glorified and exalted is He, with its great benefits, ﴿runs to a resting place for it﴾. Everything has an end, and everything has a limit leading to whom? To Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

He said: ("That" means: its running to its resting place is "the decree of the Almighty in His dominion, the All-Knowing of His creation").
﴿That﴾, that is, its running to its resting place, ﴿is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾. The decree is attributed here to this noble name ﴿the Almighty﴾ because this great sun requires power and an overpowering authority, so the name ﴿the Almighty﴾ is used. "Al-'Aziz" comprises three meanings: first, al-'Aziz in His standing (qadr), al-'Aziz in His subjugation (qahr), and al-'Aziz in His inaccessibility (imtina').

As for His standing: it means that Allah has a great dignity to which no one is equal.
As for His subjugation: it means that Allah has dominance and absolute authority. The pre-Islamic poet says:
"Where is the escape, when God is the Seeker?
And the one with the cut nose is the defeated, not the victor."
As for His inaccessibility: the meaning is that He is exempt from every deficiency and defect.

As for ﴿al-'Alim﴾ (the All-Knowing): it means the one possessing complete and comprehensive knowledge. The knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, is complete, not preceded by ignorance and not subject to forgetfulness, and comprehensive, encompassing every small and great thing. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. He knows what is in the land and the sea. Not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but it is in a clear register﴾ [al-An'am 59]. What is written in a clear register was only written after it was known to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the unknown is not written. This indicates the vastness of Allah's knowledge and that He encompasses everything in totality and in detail. So ﴿al-'Alim﴾ means the one with complete and comprehensive knowledge: its completeness lies in that it is not preceded by ignorance and is not subject to forgetfulness, and its comprehensiveness lies in that it encompasses every small and great thing.

He says: ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾. Allah mentioned these two names because of the fitness of the context, since the sun is not a trivial thing easily controlled, but a great thing that requires might and knowledge.

Then He said: ﴿And the moon﴾ [Ya-Sin 39]. "Al-qamar" has two readings: the nominative (raf') and the accusative (nasb). There are thus two grammatical possibilities: ﴿al-qamaru﴾ with the nominative, as a subject whose predicate is ﴿qaddarnahu﴾ (We have measured it). And ﴿al-qamara﴾ with the accusative, as an object of a verb that is omitted and explained by the mentioned verb, so it falls under the construction of "ishtighal" (the verb is occupied with the pronoun). Here the nominative and accusative are equally preferable, because the sentence preceding it, ﴿And the sun runs﴾, is a nominal sentence whose predicate is a verb, so both possibilities are permitted for "al-qamar." It is well known that the nominative is preferred when the topicalized element is conjoined to a nominal sentence, and the accusative is preferred when it is conjoined to a verbal sentence.

He said: (﴿And the moon﴾ in the nominative and accusative, and it is in the accusative, governed by a verb explained by what follows it). That is: it is explained by the mentioned verb, and the implied sense is: "And We measured the moon as stations." There is no need to say, as some people say: "The estimate is: And We measured the moon, We measured it." Why? Because one does not combine the explainer and the explained. If you want to estimate, say: "The estimate is: And We measured the moon, what? Stations."

If you say: Why did He not say, Mighty and Majestic: "And We measured the moon as stations"?

We say: because when He brought the nominal sentence whose predicate is a verb, it is as if He attributed this action to it twice: He attributed the verb, which is measuring, to the moon twice; once by mentioning it as an explicit noun, and once by mentioning it as a pronoun in ﴿qaddarnahu﴾.

Allah, exalted is He, said: (﴿And the moon, We have measured it﴾ in respect of its course ﴿as stations﴾). The measuring of the moon by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as stations is because by this measure it can come in this form which we observe: it changes each night from the other. Were it not for this measure, it would not change. But it is measured as stations: twenty-eight stations, according to the known stars among the Arabs, one station each night. It remains one night if the month is twenty-nine days, or two nights if it is thirty, and these two nights are called the nights of concealment (layali al-istisrar), meaning the hiding, when the moon is hidden, either at the beginning of the following month or at the end of the previous month. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And the moon, We have measured it as stations﴾ (twenty-eight stations in twenty-eight nights of each month, and it hides for two nights if the month is thirty days, and one night if it is twenty-nine days). Whoever wishes to know the details of this knowledge should read what the scholars have written about it, especially in our time, for they have discovered wondrous things about this measure.

The moon, Allah measured it as stations, one station each day. So it differs each night from what? From the other. For this reason it appears small, then grows, then returns to shrinking according to its nearness to the sun. Whenever it draws near the sun, its light weakens, because the moon's light is derived from the sun's light. It has no light of its own; it is a dark body, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, and We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day as a seeing one﴾ [al-Isra' 12]. It is a dark body that gains light only from something else. When it faces the sun, light appears in it, and the further it is from the sun, the more the facing increases, because its motion is spherical; the nearer it is, the weaker the facing, and when it rises, the facing increases. For this reason it becomes full of light when it is in the east and the sun is in the west, for the facing between them is then complete, so it fills with light.

What is the luminous part of it?

The luminous part of it is that which faces the sun. For this reason, in the winter days, when the sun is behind it, the opening of its crescent is toward the east; in the summer days, the opening of its crescent is toward the south, because the sun is to its north and it is to the south of the sun, so you find its opening toward the south. In winter, since it faces away from the sun and is behind it, you find its opening toward the east. For this reason some people err, who think that the opening of the moon, that is, the opening of its crescent, is always toward the east or toward the south. This is not correct; if you want to know this, reflect on it.

Good. He says: ﴿We have measured it as stations until it returned﴾ (in its last stations, in the eye's view) ﴿like the old date-stalk﴾ [Ya-Sin 39], that is, like the stalk of the strands of the date cluster when it has aged, for it becomes thin, curved and yellow. So until the moon returned, after the measuring of these stations, ﴿like the old date-stalk﴾. The "'urjun" is called in our colloquial language ("'urjud") with a dal; this 'urjud is the base of the strands in the spathe of the date palm, and when it dries it curves and turns yellow. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, likened the moon in visual appearance to this old stalk; that is, it appears thin, yellow and curved. Is this figurative comparison (tashbih baligh) or non-eloquent comparison? Non-eloquent, why? Because the particle of comparison is mentioned; the eloquent comparison is the one in which the particle of comparison and the point of resemblance are omitted, and if either one is mentioned, the comparison is not eloquent.

Good. He says: ﴿until it returned like the old date-stalk (39). It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day﴾ [Ya-Sin 39–40]. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned that the sun runs to a resting place for it, and that this is a decree from the Almighty, the All-Knowing, and that Allah measured the moon as stations, which it descends one station after another until, after becoming full of light, it becomes like the old date-stalk, He showed that this order can never collide, because it is decreed by whom? By Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the Almighty, the All-Knowing: stations it does not pass beyond or transgress.

He said: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon﴾. ﴿Yanbaghi﴾ means "is possible," and the author says: (it is easy and valid), but it is better to say: it means "is possible"; that is, it is not possible for the sun to overtake the moon. We have already noted that when the phrase "la yanbaghi" (it is not fitting) or "ma yanbaghi" occurs in the Qur'an, it means what is impossible in the utmost degree, as in His saying: ﴿And it is not fitting for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ [Maryam 92], meaning that this is impossible. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed Allah does not sleep, and it is not fitting for Him to sleep" [[Related by Muslim (179 / 295) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]]; that is, that is impossible.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 36, verse 37–40 (part 2 of 2):

So (...) "it is not for it (yanbaghi)" [﴿يَنْبَغِي﴾]. The original form is: "the sun, it is not fitting for it (la yanbaghi lahā)". But he placed the negation first so that what is negated is the whole nominal sentence in its entirety. He said: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon﴾. He means: it is not possible for it to catch up with the moon and so be together with it at night. For example, when it sets, it is not possible for it to rise again during the night time. If we suppose that it returns at the twelfth hour and rises at the twelfth hour, then between its setting and its rising there are twelve hours. It cannot rise at the eighth hour, so that there would be eight hours between its setting and its rising, because this would contradict the measure that God, the Mighty and Majestic, has decreed for it and by which He made it move. Why? For the perfection of God's power and the order of this universe, and that it cannot differ or be disturbed. But when the Day of Resurrection comes, the sun and the moon will be joined together, and the order of the celestial sphere will be disrupted; indeed, the whole order will change: ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come out before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ibrahim 48].

Likewise He said: ﴿Nor does the night overtake the day﴾. He means: the night does not precede the day; rather, it only comes after it.

Here He said: ﴿Nor does the night overtake the day﴾, as if the night were the one that could precede the day, so God, the Mighty and Majestic, negated that the night could overtake the day.

It has been said: the meaning is that the night does not come before the end of the day. So God, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the sunrise in His saying: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon﴾, meaning: it is not possible for the sun to rise at night. ﴿Nor does the night overtake the day﴾: it is not possible for the night to come during the time of the day. So if we suppose that the sun sets at the twelfth hour, it is not possible for it to set at the ninth hour, for example, because if it set at the ninth hour the night would overtake the day, even in some part of it. It has also been said: the meaning of ﴿Nor does the night overtake the day﴾ is: the night does not take the place of the day so that two nights follow each other equally. The meaning is correct according to both opinions. It is not possible for the night to come while some of the day remains, and it is not possible for the whole night to come in the place of the day, because this would contradict the decree of God, the Mighty and Majestic, who described Himself as the Mighty, and named Himself the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

He said: ﴿And each is in an orbit, swimming﴾ [Ya-Sin 40] (the tanwin on ﴿each﴾ is a replacement for the genitive noun to which it refers: of the sun, the moon and the stars). The stars are not mentioned here; the correct reading is: of the sun and the moon, since there is no mention of the stars here. (﴿in an orbit﴾ circular ﴿swimming﴾ moving.) He means: each of the sun, the moon, the night and the day swims in an orbit. The orbit (falak) is the circular thing, and from it comes the whorl (falakat) of the spindle: the whorl of the spindle is the round part at its top. Perhaps you have seen the spindle with which women spin wool; at its top there is something like a round disc, that is the whorl of the spindle.

The orbit is circular, in which the sun, the moon, the night and the day revolve. His saying ﴿swimming﴾ means: moving. But the meaning is more precise than what the author said, because sabh is swimming in water. It is as if these are floating in a wide orbit, revolving; they are not moving on a flat earth or on water, but they swim in this horizon.

* * *

* (...) The noble verse: this is a great verse about the night, in which He strips the day from it as the skin is stripped from a sheep, and this indicates that it comes little by little.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: the original state is darkness, by His saying: ﴿We strip the day from it﴾ [Ya-Sin 37]. This indicates that the original state is darkness and that the day is something that comes upon it, and therefore it is stripped from it. And this is so, for the origin of light is the sun, and the sun is something new that arrives upon the night. So the original is darkness, and the light comes after it.

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: reminding creation of this blessing, by His saying: ﴿then they are in darkness﴾ [Ya-Sin 37]. And that if it were not for God's blessing upon us in this day which is stripped from the night, we would always be in darkness, and this is without doubt tiring to people and harmful to them. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then hear?"﴾ [al-Qasas 71].

Then He said: ﴿And the sun runs on to its resting place﴾ to the end of the verses.

* Among its benefits: the sun runs, that is, moves, and this is the reality. The apparent meaning of the noble Qur'an is that its motion is by its own nature, and it is not meant that it runs in the sense of appearance to the eye while the one that revolves is the earth. It is obligatory to take the Qur'an according to its apparent meaning until a clear proof is established that would be for us a proof before God, the Mighty and Majestic, if we depart from the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, because the one who spoke the Qur'an is the Creator, the Mighty and Majestic, and He is the All-Knowing of His creation. So if He says that the sun runs, it is obligatory for us to say that the sun runs, and it is not permissible for us to say that we are the ones who run; rather, it is the sun that runs by the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

* Among its benefits: this sun, which is constantly and continuously moving, must have an end, by His saying: ﴿to its resting place﴾. Following from this, all creatures have an end: everything in this world of creatures has an end and will pass away: ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come out before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ibrahim 48].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: this sun is measured with a far-reaching, ordered measure, by His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾. This reality bears witness to it: from the time Allah created this sun until it ceases, it is in its orbit and does not advance or delay from the course which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded it to follow, and it does not rise or sink. It has even been said: if it sank by the width of a hair, it would burn the earth, and if it rose by the width of a hair, the earth would freeze. But God, the Mighty and Majestic, made it according to this wondrous, firm measure that does not change.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of two of Allah's names, namely: ﴿the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾. From them is derived the affirmation of two attributes that they include, namely might and knowledge. From them is also derived the affirmation of the effect or the judgement, which is that He overcomes everyone and knows everything.

* Among the benefits of the verse in His saying: ﴿And the moon — We have decreed for it stations﴾, among its benefits also: that this moon is a sign of the signs of God, the Mighty and Majestic, in that it is placed in its orbit, and yet it has stations which it descends to each night. It is not unrestricted, but it is measured by stations which it descends to each night. The wisdom of these stations is that people may know the number of years and the reckoning, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is He who made the sun a brightness and the moon a light and determined for it stations that you may know the number of years and the account﴾ [Yunus 5]. So much so that those who know the stations of the moon know the night of the month, even if they had not calculated from the beginning, on the basis of knowing the stations, because these stations do not change, and the moon's arrival at them also does not change. They are arranged by God, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of analogy (qiyas), by His saying: ﴿until it returns like the old dried palm-stalk﴾. Every simile or parable in the Qur'an indicates analogy, because a simile or parable is attaching one thing to another for a reason, which is called in rhetoric the aspect of comparison (wajh al-shabah).

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: applying the word "old" (qadim) to other than God, contrary to the philosophers who say: the most specific attribute of God is antiquity (qidam). This is wrong; if this were the most specific attribute of God, it would not be described by anything other than God. Antiquity does not indicate eternity (azaliyya). For this palm-stalk God described it as old, yet it is not, what? It is not eternal, since it is a created thing that did not exist before. Through this the falsity of the saying of those who claim that the most specific attribute of God, the Mighty and Majestic, is antiquity becomes clear. If they had said: the most specific attribute of God is primacy (awwaliyya), we would agree with what they said, because God is the First, before whom there is nothing. But to say that antiquity is the most specific attribute of God, while it is also applied to what is created, this is not possible and not correct.

* Also in it: there is evidence of God's power in respect of the light of the moon, for it begins weak, then increases in strength, then returns to weakness. This is from the power of God, the Mighty and Majestic, for if He willed He could make it always full and complete, or always deficient.

* Also among its benefits: an allusion to the state of man. When a person reflects upon the moon, he finds that it corresponds to the state of man, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is Allah who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾ [al-Rum 54]. The state of man is thus exactly equivalent to the state of the moon: the moon appears weak, then increases in strength, until when its strength is complete it begins to decline, and likewise man with respect to his life.

God, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night overtake the day﴾.

* In this verse there is evidence that the sunnah (law/pattern) of God, the Mighty and Majestic, does not change; this is the basic principle, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you will not find in the sunnah of Allah any alteration, and you will not find in the sunnah of Allah any transformation﴾ [Fatir 43]. So the sunnah of God, glorified and exalted, does not change in the universe. But is it a necessary sunnah, such that it is impossible for God to change it?

The answer: No. But God, the Exalted, has informed us that this sunnah does not change, yet it changes by His changing it. For this reason the sun was held back for Yusha' ibn Nun[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3124), and Muslim (1747/32), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], as came in the authentic hadiths. And for this reason too, when the Hour draws near, the sun will rise from where? From its place of setting. And for this reason the moon was split in the time of the Prophet ﷺ and became two halves[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3636), and Muslim (2800/43), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]]. These cosmic sunan do not alter and do not change, but God is able to alter or change them, and this would be for a cause.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the sun cannot rise at night. It cannot, according to the divine sunnah; but according to God's power, what? It is possible for it to rise at night, because God says: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: the night does not precede the day, so it does not enter upon it or come before it in such a way that two nights follow each other entirely: ﴿Nor does the night overtake the day﴾. This is what appears to us from this noble verse, and it may have a meaning other than what we understand from its outward form. For this reason, perhaps, those who study astronomy may see in this expression more than what has become clear to us.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse also: the sun, the moon, the night and the day are in an orbit — that is, in something circular like the whorl of a spindle — and they revolve; as He says: ﴿each in an orbit, swimming﴾.

* Among its benefits: the weakness of the saying of those who claim that the sun is in the fourth heaven and the moon in the lowest heaven, and who make the planets, the sun and the moon specific planets, each in a heaven, in this order from highest to lowest:
Zuhal, Sharā, his Mirrikh from his Shams, so Tazāharat with ʿUtārid the moons.
These are seven, each one in a heaven: Zuhal (Saturn) is the highest, in the seventh heaven, according to the words of the earlier astronomers; Sharā (Jupiter) in the sixth heaven; Mirrikh (Mars) in the fifth heaven; Shams (the sun) in the fourth heaven; Tazāharat (Venus) in the third heaven; ʿUtārid (Mercury) in the second heaven; al-Aqmār (the moon) in the lowest heaven. This verse contains the order of these planets:
Zuhal, Sharā, his Mirrikh from his Shams, so Tazāharat with ʿUtārid the moons.

(...) from the Book of God nor from the Sunnah of the Messenger of God ﷺ. We only know that these planets are above one another through eclipse: if the moon eclipses the sun, we know that it is beneath it, just as we know that cloud is beneath the sun because it screens it. And if the moon eclipses some of the stars, we know that it — that is, the moon — is beneath them. For this reason the moon eclipses all the stars, and the sun, and nothing eclipses it except the earth, because the earth is beneath it and blocks the light of the sun from it, and then it is eclipsed. I and others have witnessed that the moon eclipses some stars: you find it moving around them and then covering them. This shows that the moon is lower than the rank or height of these stars.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: a refutation of the saying of those who claim that the sun is fixed and does not revolve. The strange thing is that they say it is fixed and that the moon revolves around the earth. This is an error, because God, glorified and exalted, made the ruling one: He said: ﴿each in an orbit, swimming﴾. So if we interpret swimming as revolving and affirm that for the moon, then let us affirm it for the sun too.

I have a word here which we have not explained from the author's commentary; he said: (they swim; they were given the status of rational beings).

(They were given the status of whom?) The sun, the moon, the night and the day (were given the status of rational beings), and that is by using the wāw which is for rational beings. The wāw is the plural pronoun, which only comes for rational beings; for non-rational beings the plural is with the feminine plural nūn. So if we want to add something to non-rational things in the plural, we use the feminine plural nūn; and for rational beings we use the wāw or the mīm. For example, you say: "the camels — their riders mounted them", not "the camels — their riders mounted them" with the mīm, because the mīm is for the rational. And you say: "the camels came (qadimna)" or "the camels drank (sharibna)", and you do not say "they drank" (sharibū), because the wāw here is for the rational. ﴿yasbahūn﴾ came with the wāw which is for the rational; he says: it has been given the status of a rational being by attributing swimming and moving to it, and moving only comes from one with will and reason.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 36, verse 41–42:

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring⦗dhurriyyatahum⦘ (and in another reading ﴿dhurriyyatihim﴾; i.e., their forefathers, the ancestors) ﴿in the laden ship⦗al-fulk⦘﴾ (i.e., the ship of Noah) ﴿al-mashhun⦗the laden⦘﴾ [Ya-Sin 41], meaning the filled, ﴿and We created for them the like of it⦗mithlihi⦘﴾ (i.e., the like of Noah's ship), which is what they made in its form, of small and large vessels, by the teaching of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿that they ride⦘﴾ [Ya-Sin 42].

﴿A sign for them⦘﴾, i.e., for all people. For what? The author says: (for Our power). We affirm that, but there is also in it a sign of another matter, which is the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, toward creation and His blessings upon them. So it is a sign for us indicating the power of Allah, His mercy and His favour upon us. This ship, which Allah has subjected, runs upon the sea, carrying provisions from one place to another, carrying people, carrying livestock, and carrying everything in which lies our benefit. This is among the signs that point to the power of the Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and to His mercy.

His saying ﴿that We carried their offspring⦘ is a clause in the sense of a verbal noun, which is the subject (mubtada'); meaning: and a sign for them is Our carrying of their offspring.

Regarding ﴿dhurriyyatahum⦘ and ﴿dhurriyyatihim⦘, the author said: (i.e., their forefathers, the ancestors), thus making the meaning of "offspring" here the ancestors, i.e., the fathers, even though what is well known in the Arabic language is that dhurriyyah refers to descendants and not to fathers, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We indeed sent Noah and Abraham, and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Scripture⦘ [al-Hadid 26]. The author and those who follow his view in interpreting the verse say that dhurriyyah is a term shared between ancestors and descendants, since it is derived from (dhara'a, to create), and creating applies to both ancestors and descendants. Then they also say that the context of the verse indicates this: ﴿a sign for them that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾. The young ones present with them, when they are carried, will be carried along with them. And if the meaning of offspring were those who come after, how would that be a sign, when it is not witnessed by them? Thus it is necessary that the meaning of offspring be the ancestors, because the young ones whose carrying is witnessed are carried as the carrying of their fathers, since usually they are carried only with their fathers; and the young ones not witnessed who come later would not be a sign for whom? For those who did not witness it. Therefore it is necessary that the meaning of offspring be the fathers.

This view of the author agrees with the apparent meaning of the verse, but it opposes what was customary in the Arabic language, that dhurriyyah refers to descendants. For this reason some scholars held that the pronoun here refers to the kind and not the individual; the meaning being: ﴿their offspring⦘, i.e., the offspring of their kind, such as Noah for example. Noah, peace be upon him, is of our kind, a human being, a son of Adam, so Allah carried his offspring in the laden ship. They said: this is not impossible in the Arabic language; ﴿And We indeed created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a drop in a firm lodging⦘ [al-Mu'minun 12, 13]. ﴿We placed him⦘, i.e., the kind of man and not his individual, because the one placed as a drop—is it Adam who was created from the extract, or another? Another, without doubt. So the pronoun returned to Adam by way of the kind. Therefore the pronoun in His saying ﴿their offspring⦘ returns to those present by way of what? By way of the kind.

So who is the kind? They said: it is Noah, since he is a human being, and his offspring are those carried. So the meaning of ﴿that We carried their offspring⦘ is: the offspring of their kind, namely Noah, peace be upon him. His offspring were carried in the laden ship, and there was created for them the like of it, which they ride. This is very close and does not oppose the apparent meaning of the verse, and it points to the fact that this ship was made a sign for those after Noah to take heed from and to build from. His saying, the Exalted, in Surat al-Qamar: ﴿And We have left it as a sign; so is there any who will remember?⦘ [al-Qamar 15].

There is a third opinion, God willing, we will discuss it tomorrow. Yes.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, this is not correct. Yes, this is not correct. Those who said that eclipses occur at any time, and Allah is capable of all things, we say: this is not correct, because Allah, the Exalted, has established the custom that there is no eclipse of the sun except on the nights of concealment at the end of the month, and no eclipse of the moon except on the nights of full moon. And the saying of some of the imams, that if an eclipse occurs at 'Arafah after the sun has set, one should pray and then depart, is to be said: this is a hypothetical matter and does not occur, and it is not possible for this to happen.

* Student: They argue that the sun was eclipsed on the day al-Husayn died, and he died on the tenth of Muharram.

* The Shaykh: Al-Husayn?

* Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: This is not correct; either the eclipse is not correct or the date is not correct. They also argue that it was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim died. This is correct: it was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim died. They say Ibrahim died on the tenth of Rabi' al-Awwal. This is also not correct; the correct view is that the sun was eclipsed on the twenty-ninth of Shawwal. On this basis there is no difficulty in the matter. Yes, this is not possible, because this is a consistent sunnah and cannot differ, unless it is a sign. If it is a sign, there is no harm, such as the splitting of the moon. For this reason we affirm that the moon was truly split, unlike some contemporaries who denied the splitting of the moon and said: the moon is among the celestial spheres and can never change at all, and that the meaning of the splitting of the moon is the manifestation of the Prophet's ﷺ message, in the sense of the moon's clarity, i.e., the light of the message. They also argue that if this event were real, it would have been world-famous in history; it is no small matter for the moon to split and people not to know of it except the people of Makkah or those around them. All these are weak and false justifications, because the splitting of the moon is well known, indeed mass-transmitted (mutawatir) from the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the Qur'an indicates it: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And if they see a sign, they turn away⦘ [al-Qamar 1, 2]. That it did not become world-famous in history does not prevent its occurring in reality, for it may have happened during the day—this is with regard to those around them—then there may have been clouds and obstacles that prevented it, then it may have occurred at night while they were asleep. The point is that there are obstacles. Moreover, its splitting did not last the whole night; it split until the Prophet, peace be upon him, showed them this sign, then it rejoined, and this may have lasted only about five minutes or so.

﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship (41). And We created for them the like of it that they ride﴾. The Exalted said: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried⦘. Where is the subject in this verse?

* Student: The verbal noun clause.

* The Shaykh: The verbal noun clause. What is the estimated form?

* Student: Their carrying.

* The Shaykh: (...) for the descendants, so we say: the meaning of offspring here is the offspring of Noah, and it is attributed to these people by way of the kind; i.e., We carried the offspring of their kind in the laden ship. We mentioned for this a parallel, which is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We indeed created man from an extract of clay (12). Then We placed him as a drop﴾ [al-Mu'minun 12, 13]. It is not "We made the man who was created from the extract" a drop, because the man created from the extract is Adam, and he cannot be a drop in a firm lodging; rather, what becomes a drop in a firm lodging is what is of his kind. This view is the one the soul is at rest with and which the context does not reject.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿in the laden ship⦘. This is the beginning of the lesson now. (﴿in the ship⦘, i.e., the ship of Noah), so the "al-" here is for mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni), since no prior mention of it has preceded, and it is not for generalization (al-istighraq), because what is meant by it is one single ship. So the "al-" here is for mental reference, i.e., the ship known to your minds, which is the one Allah the Exalted said to Noah: ﴿Build the ship under Our eyes﴾ [al-Mu'minun 27]. The ship, as has passed with us, is applied to the collective and also to the singular. Its application to the singular is as in this verse, and to the collective as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿until when you are in the ships and they sail with them by a favourable wind﴾ [Yunus 22]. ﴿They sail⦘ refers to the ships, and this pronoun is a plural pronoun and does not refer to the singular. For this reason some jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, said: the hunchback whose hump is like bowing intends bowing. He said: this is like (fulk) in Arabic, one does not know whether it is plural or singular except by intention. So the hunchback, bent of back, how does he bow by intention? He intends bowing, because he is still a hunched bower.

﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship⦘ (i.e., the ship of Noah; ﴿al-mashhun⦘, i.e., the filled), filled with whom? Filled with human beings who believed with Noah: ﴿And none believed with him except a few⦘ [Hud 40]; filled with the rest of the animals, because Allah said: ﴿We said: carry in it of each kind two, a pair﴾ [Hud 40].

And His saying: ﴿And We created for them the like of it⦘ (i.e., the like of Noah's ship, which is what they made in its form, of small and large vessels). Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reminds them first of the carrying of their earlier forefathers, who are the offspring of Noah, and second that Allah the Exalted created for them from the like of these ships what they ride; as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We have left it as a sign; so is there any who will remember?⦘ [al-Qamar 15]. So people learned how to build ships and began to make ships like this one. Perhaps His saying in Surat al-Qamar: ﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and nails⦘ [al-Qamar 13] contains an indication of the materials of this ship or this vessel, so that people may learn; for He did not say, "We carried him upon a ship," but said: ﴿upon one of planks and nails⦘, as if saying: this ship is made of planks and nails, so that people may learn the materials of this ship.

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And We created for them the like of it that they ride⦘ [Ya-Sin 42]. ﴿The like of it⦘: what is meant by the like here is the kind, not resemblance in every respect; for resemblance in every respect may be impossible. The kind suffices, whereas the species varies with the ages; each age has its own type of ships, and ships have continued to advance on the seas until they reached what they have reached in our present age.

The author, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: (by the teaching of Allah the Exalted). This points to an implied question; as if he said: how does Allah the Exalted say ﴿And We created for them the like of it⦘, when these ships are made by human hands, and are not the creation of Allah, like the creation of the camel that is ridden, and the horse and the like? The author answered that Allah the Exalted ascribed their making to Himself because it was by His teaching.

* Among the benefits of this verse:

* First: the clarification of what there was in the salvation of mankind from drowning in the time of Noah; for had Allah not preserved these people, mankind would have vanished from the earth. But Allah the Exalted preserved Noah and those with him. Yet of the descendants of those who were with him, none remained except the descendants of Noah alone, as Allah said: ﴿And We made his offspring the remaining ones⦘ [al-Saffat 77]. As for others, none of them remained, and for this reason Noah is called the second father of mankind.

* Second, among the benefits of this noble verse: the clarification of Allah's blessing in what He bestowed upon these people by teaching them the ships they ride on the sea. Had it not been for these ships, no one could have crossed from one dry land to another separated by water; but Allah taught them the making of these, until they reached what they reached.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the ship in which Noah was contained human beings and others, as shown by His saying: ﴿the laden⦘.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that likeness does not necessarily require equality in every respect; as shown by His saying: ﴿the like of it⦘. These ships that exist, and those that existed at the time the Qur'an was revealed, are not like Noah's ship in every respect. What indicates that likeness does not require equality in every respect is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth their like⦘ [al-Talaq 12]; for the likeness here is in number only, otherwise the great differences between the earth and the heavens are manifest.

* And in His saying: ﴿that they ride⦘ there is an indication of the comfort gained through these ships, and that the place of riding is for settledness. Therefore there is also in it a clarification of a blessing from Allah, glorified and exalted, through the settledness of the riders on these ships.

Another, without doubt. So the pronoun returned to Adam by way of the kind. Therefore the pronoun in His saying ﴿their offspring⦘ returns to those present by way of what? By way of the kind.

So the meaning of ﴿that We carried their offspring⦘ is: the offspring of their kind, namely Noah, peace be upon him. His offspring were carried in the laden ship, and there was created for them the like of it, which they ride. This is very close and does not oppose the apparent meaning of the verse, and it points to the fact that this ship was made a sign for those after Noah to take heed from and to build from. His saying, the Exalted, in Surat al-Qamar: ﴿And We have left it as a sign; so is there any who will remember?⦘ [al-Qamar 15].

There is a third opinion, God willing, we will discuss it tomorrow. Yes.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, this is not correct. Yes, this is not correct. Those who said that eclipses occur at any time, and Allah is capable of all things, we say: this is not correct, because Allah, the Exalted, has established the custom that there is no eclipse of the sun except on the nights of concealment at the end of the month, and no eclipse of the moon except on the nights of full moon. And the saying of some of the imams, that if an eclipse occurs at 'Arafah after the sun has set, one should pray and then depart, is to be said: this is a hypothetical matter and does not occur, and it is not possible for this to happen.

* Student: They argue that the sun was eclipsed on the day al-Husayn died, and he died on the tenth of Muharram.

* The Shaykh: Al-Husayn?

* Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: This is not correct; either the eclipse is not correct or the date is not correct. They also argue that it was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim died. This is correct: it was eclipsed on the day Ibrahim died. They say Ibrahim died on the tenth of Rabi' al-Awwal. This is also not correct; the correct view is that the sun was eclipsed on the twenty-ninth of Shawwal. On this basis there is no difficulty in the matter. Yes, this is not possible, because this is a consistent sunnah and cannot differ, unless it is a sign. If it is a sign, there is no harm, such as the splitting of the moon. For this reason we affirm that the moon was truly split, unlike some contemporaries who denied the splitting of the moon and said: the moon is among the celestial spheres and can never change at all, and that the meaning of the splitting of the moon is the manifestation of the Prophet's ﷺ message, in the sense of the moon's clarity, i.e., the light of the message. They also argue that if this event were real, it would have been world-famous in history; it is no small matter for the moon to split and people not to know of it except the people of Makkah or those around them. All these are weak and false justifications, because the splitting of the moon is well known, indeed mass-transmitted (mutawatir) from the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the Qur'an indicates it: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And if they see a sign, they turn away⦘ [al-Qamar 1, 2]. That it did not become world-famous in history does not prevent its occurring in reality, for it may have happened during the day—this is with regard to those around them—then there may have been clouds and obstacles that prevented it, then it may have occurred at night while they were asleep. The point is that there are obstacles. Moreover, its splitting did not last the whole night; it split until the Prophet, peace be upon him, showed them this sign, then it rejoined, and this may have lasted only about five minutes or so.

﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship (41). And We created for them the like of it that they ride﴾. The Exalted said: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried⦘. Where is the subject in this verse?

* Student: The verbal noun clause.

* The Shaykh: The verbal noun clause. What is the estimated form?

* Student: Their carrying.

* The Shaykh: (...) for the descendants, so we say: the meaning of offspring here is the offspring of Noah, and it is attributed to these people by way of the kind; i.e., We carried the offspring of their kind in the laden ship. We mentioned for this a parallel, which is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We indeed created man from an extract of clay (12). Then We placed him as a drop﴾ [al-Mu'minun 12, 13]. It is not "We made the man who was created from the extract" a drop, because the man created from the extract is Adam, and he cannot be a drop in a firm lodging; rather, what becomes a drop in a firm lodging is what is of his kind. This view is the one the soul is at rest with and which the context does not reject.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿in the laden ship⦘. This is the beginning of the lesson now. (﴿in the ship⦘, i.e., the ship of Noah), so the "al-" here is for mental reference (al-'ahd al-dhihni), since no prior mention of it has preceded, and it is not for generalization (al-istighraq), because what is meant by it is one single ship. So the "al-" here is for mental reference, i.e., the ship known to your minds, which is the one Allah the Exalted said to Noah: ﴿Build the ship under Our eyes﴾ [al-Mu'minun 27]. The ship, as has passed with us, is applied to the collective and also to the singular. Its application to the singular is as in this verse, and to the collective as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿until when you are in the ships and they sail with them by a favourable wind﴾ [Yunus 22]. ﴿They sail⦘ refers to the ships, and this pronoun is a plural pronoun and does not refer to the singular. For this reason some jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, said: the hunchback whose hump is like bowing intends bowing. He said: this is like (fulk) in Arabic, one does not know whether it is plural or singular except by intention. So the hunchback, bent of back, how does he bow by intention? He intends bowing, because he is still a hunched bower.

﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship⦘ (i.e., the ship of Noah; ﴿al-mashhun⦘, i.e., the filled), filled with whom? Filled with human beings who believed with Noah: ﴿And none believed with him except a few⦘ [Hud 40]; filled with the rest of the animals, because Allah said: ﴿We said: carry in it of each kind two, a pair﴾ [Hud 40].

And His saying: ﴿And We created for them the like of it⦘ (i.e., the like of Noah's ship, which is what they made in its form, of small and large vessels). Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reminds them first of the carrying of their earlier forefathers, who are the offspring of Noah, and second that Allah the Exalted created for them from the like of these ships what they ride; as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We have left it as a sign; so is there any who will remember?⦘ [al-Qamar 15]. So people learned how to build ships and began to make ships like this one. Perhaps His saying in Surat al-Qamar: ﴿And We carried him upon one of planks and nails⦘ [al-Qamar 13] contains an indication of the materials of this ship or this vessel, so that people may learn; for He did not say, "We carried him upon a ship," but said: ﴿upon one of planks and nails⦘, as if saying: this ship is made of planks and nails, so that people may learn the materials of this ship.

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And We created for them the like of it that they ride⦘ [Ya-Sin 42]. ﴿The like of it⦘: what is meant by the like here is the kind, not resemblance in every respect; for resemblance in every respect may be impossible. The kind suffices, whereas the species varies with the ages; each age has its own type of ships, and ships have continued to advance on the seas until they reached what they have reached in our present age.

The author, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: (by the teaching of Allah the Exalted). This points to an implied question; as if he said: how does Allah the Exalted say ﴿And We created for them the like of it⦘, when these ships are made by human hands, and are not the creation of Allah, like the creation of the camel that is ridden, and the horse and the like? The author answered that Allah the Exalted ascribed their making to Himself because it was by His teaching.

* Among the benefits of this verse:

* First: the clarification of what there was in the salvation of mankind from drowning in the time of Noah; for had Allah not preserved these people, mankind would have vanished from the earth. But Allah the Exalted preserved Noah and those with him. Yet of the descendants of those who were with him, none remained except the descendants of Noah alone, as Allah said: ﴿And We made his offspring the remaining ones⦘ [al-Saffat 77]. As for others, none of them remained, and for this reason Noah is called the second father of mankind.

* Second, among the benefits of this noble verse: the clarification of Allah's blessing in what He bestowed upon these people by teaching them the ships they ride on the sea. Had it not been for these ships, no one could have crossed from one dry land to another separated by water; but Allah taught them the making of these, until they reached what they reached.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the ship in which Noah was contained human beings and others, as shown by His saying: ﴿the laden⦘.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that likeness does not necessarily require equality in every respect; as shown by His saying: ﴿the like of it⦘. These ships that exist, and those that existed at the time the Qur'an was revealed, are not like Noah's ship in every respect. What indicates that likeness does not require equality in every respect is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth their like⦘ [al-Talaq 12]; for the likeness here is in number only, otherwise the great differences between the earth and the heavens are manifest.

* And in His saying: ﴿that they ride⦘ there is an indication of the comfort gained through these ships, and that the place of riding is for settledness. Therefore there is also in it a clarification of a blessing from Allah, glorified and exalted, through the settledness of the riders on these ships.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if We wish, We drown them, and there is no one to call for help for them, nor are they rescued (43) except as a mercy from Us and as enjoyment for a time.﴾ [Ya-Sin 43–44].

In the verse there is a conditional sentence: its condition is ﴿nasha'﴾ (We wish), and its response is ﴿nughriqhum﴾ (We drown them). There is also an exceptive construction (istithna' mufarragh) from the most general of states, namely His words ﴿illa rahmatan minna﴾ (except as a mercy from Us), where it is a object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi); that is: except for the sake of the mercy that comes from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And if We wish, We drown them﴾, meaning: when they board the ships, and the matter is as such. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And among His signs are the ships in the sea, like mountains (32). If He wills, He stills the wind, and they remain motionless upon its surface. Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful one (33). Or He causes them to perish for what they have earned, and pardons much.﴾ [ash-Shura 32–34]. Thus Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, warned of two matters concerning these ships: either He stills the wind so that they remain motionless upon its surface, or He drowns them.

Here He says: ﴿And if We wish, We drown them﴾, while they are in their ships, ﴿there is no one to call for help for them﴾. The ﴿sarikh﴾ (one who calls for help) means the one who rescues, and the rescuer is called ﴿sarikh﴾ because it is customary that when a person is attacked by someone, he cries out seeking help. From this is the hadith about the Battle of Badr, that Abu Sufyan sent a crier (sarikh) to the people of Makkah to seek their help.[[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (9727) from the hadith of ʿIkrimah, the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbas.]]

He said: ﴿nor are they rescued﴾ (yunjawn), meaning: no one aids them and no one rescues them when Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, wishes to drown them.

﴿Except as a mercy from Us and as enjoyment for a time﴾: meaning, no one saves them except the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The exception here has been said to be disjunctive (munqati'), because His words ﴿nor are they rescued (43) except as a mercy from Us﴾ mean: rather, by Our mercy they are saved and rescued.

His words ﴿and as enjoyment for a time﴾ mean that they are given enjoyment until the time of their term, because Allah, the Exalted, has set a measure for everything. (That is: nothing saves them except Our mercy toward them and Our granting them enjoyment of their pleasures until the end of their terms.)

In the noble verse there are benefits:

* Among them: affirmation of the will of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from His words ﴿And if We wish, We drown them﴾.

* Among them: that when Allah intends evil for a people, there is no repelling it, from His words ﴿so there is no one to call for help for them, nor are they rescued﴾.

* Among them: the demonstration of Allah's blessing, glory be to Him and exalted, in saving them from drowning, and that their deliverance from drowning is not by their own earning and deeds, but is from the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among them: that Allah, the Exalted, may rescue a person from destruction until his term comes, from His words ﴿and as enjoyment for a time﴾.

* Among them: that remaining forever in this world is impossible and unattainable, from His words ﴿for a time﴾, and whatever has an end must come to an end.

* Among them: that a person must view the blessings of Allah, the Exalted, in being rescued from hardships or in obtaining what he loves, as a bounty from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, not by his own earning, but from Allah, from His words ﴿And if We wish, We drown them, so there is no one to call for help for them﴾.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if We wish, We drown them, and there is no one to call for help for them, nor are they rescued (43) except as a mercy from Us and as enjoyment for a time.﴾ [Ya-Sin 43–44].
